areaPack.title: Stone Court
areaPack.howToEdit: RUNTIME CONTENT: the game loads this file as the source of truth for this area. Change player-facing text in place inside each <lesson>. Stable id attributes (ph-father, …) are engine keys — do not rename without a migration. Three tiers per fact: <easy easyOrder="N">, <medium>, and <hard> — each with <learn>, <match>, and <hold>. Easy Learn: shortStory/mainIdea/loci. Medium Learn: mediumTeach (clearer than Hard, richer than Easy). Hard Learn: hardTeach/fullTeach. Held claim·reason·source stay plain and identical on all three. Hold level-up: see hold @levelUpTo / @onFail and index <holdRules>. Empty optional elements are intentional. Escape & < > in text.

meta.title: Silver City — Stone Court
meta.subtitle: Outside names for Christ
meta.blurb: A stone court of old names: Tacitus, Josephus, Pliny — Christ named by writers who were not the church.
meta.notes: Runtime/build content pack. After the Easy door, a new street: ancient-first source-dig. Engine maps lesson fields 1:1 to Learn / Match / Hold / Journal / street.

learn.hardTeach: Tacitus, Annals 15.44. Nero’s fire in Rome. To shift the blame, Nero punishes people called Christians. Tacitus pauses to explain the name: Christus, from whom the name had its origin, suffered the extreme penalty during the reign of Tiberius at the hands of one of our procurators, Pontius Pilate. He is hostile. He is not a Gospel writer. He still names Christ under Pilate, and he says the movement then broke out again in Rome. Do not claim Tacitus wrote the tomb. Hold the Roman name.

journal.title: A Roman names Christus
journal.p: Tacitus names Christus executed under Pontius Pilate. A Roman historian wrote the movement spread to Rome. He does not write the empty tomb. He still names Christ.
The Gospels already name Pilate. Tacitus is an outside voice who names the same public death.

learn.hardTeach: Josephus, Antiquities 20.9.1 (§200). High priest Ananus has James stoned. Josephus identifies him as “the brother of Jesus, who was called Christ.” Almost every serious reader grants this sentence. Antiquities 18.63–64 (the Testimonium Flavianum) is a different paragraph. Later Christian touches there are disputed. Easy Hold does not rest on that fight. Hold the James line: an outside writer names Jesus called Christ.

learn.hardTeach: Pliny the Younger, Letters 10.96–97. Around AD 112 a provincial governor writes Trajan. He has tortured deaconesses. He has learned the pattern: they meet on a stated day before dawn, sing a hymn to Christ as to a god, bind themselves not to crime, then eat a common meal. Trajan answers: do not hunt them out. If accused and they persist, punish. Christ’s name is already a public Roman problem — not a secret club Pliny invented. The churches already sang to Christ. Pliny overheard the practice from the outside.
